memoryText: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Psalm 51:10 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is a prayer for those who have discovered that their problem is deeper than their behavior. David asks God not simply to forgive what he has done but to change who he is.

“Create.” The Hebrew verb is bara, used in Genesis 1:1 for God’s making of the heavens and earth. Only God creates. David is saying that he cannot produce a clean heart on his own. No amount of effort, resolution, or discipline will do it. It must be a gift, a work of God’s creative power.

“A clean heart.” In the Bible, the heart is the center of the person: thoughts, desires, will, and affections. A clean heart is a heart purified of whatever defiles. David knows that the root of his sin was not an isolated action but the condition of his heart.

“Renew a right spirit.” The word “renew” implies that something steadfast once existed and has been lost. He asks for a spirit that is firm and fixed in the right direction, one that will not waver.

“Within me.” The work must be inward. Religion that changes only the surface is not enough. This is what the prophets promised in the new covenant: “I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you” (Ezekiel 36:26).

For the Christian, this prayer is answered at conversion and continues through sanctification. We are born again (John 3:3-6), and the Spirit is at work making us new. Yet we keep praying this prayer, because we are still being made clean. Pray it daily.
weekInReview: This week took David from the heights to the depths. You read the early Psalm 51 in its setting, David’s prayer after Nathan’s confrontation. You saw the family consequences of his sin: the assault on Tamar, Absalom’s murder of Amnon, and Absalom’s rebellion. You followed David out of Jerusalem, weeping, with his head covered, and saw how God worked behind the scenes through Hushai. You read the psalms of the wilderness, with Psalm 63’s thirst and Psalm 61’s cry from the end of the earth. You saw Absalom die and David grieve, and his gracious restoration. The week taught that forgiveness does not erase consequences, that God works through human frailty, and that the human heart needs to be re-created by God.
reflectionQuestions: David prayed for a clean heart because he saw that his problem went deeper than behavior. What do you see about your heart that behavior changes alone cannot fix?
David wished he could have died in place of his son, but could not. How does Jesus, who did die in our place, answer the grief behind that cry?
Psalm 63 says God’s steadfast love is better than life. In what areas of life do you find it hardest to believe that?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to create in you a clean heart.
Thank him for the Son who died in your place.
Rest in him, asking him to satisfy your soul.
